title: Owner-edge clobber in executeInstall is now reachable on the routine replace path
description:
From TASK-182's gating review (MEDIUM-3), disclosed by the developer and confirmed by the reviewer. **Latent today, not live — but newly reachable, which is why it needs a ticket rather than silence.**

**The defect.** `src/pack-apply.js:437-456`'s `executeInstall` writes `lock.resources[id] = { …, owners: [] }` and then calls `addOwner` for the current run's pack. Any owner edge belonging to a *different* pack is dropped in the process.

**Why it matters now.** Before TASK-182 this was only reachable on the unusual staged-but-not-live install path. TASK-182 made `plan.replace` execute through the same `executeInstall`, putting it on the **routine live-resource path** — every future plugin-wins retire runs through it.

**Verified not live today**, and the ticket should not overstate it: no multi-owner entries exist in any lockfile, the two built-in packs (`design-power`, `watch`) declare disjoint resources, and `reconcilePack` re-plans per pack against a freshly-read lock. So no consumer can currently lose an edge.

**Why it is still worth closing.** A dropped owner edge transitively breaks a guarantee the reconciler documents elsewhere: `executeRemove` promises a still-owned resource is never deleted. If pack A's edge is silently dropped while pack B replaces a shared resource, a later orphan check sees a resource that looks unowned and becomes eligible for removal — the failure surfaces far from the cause, in a different pack's run, as a deleted working skill.

The condition that makes it live is simply two packs declaring the same resource id, which is a supported shape the descriptor schema does not forbid.

**Fix direction (decide, do not assume):** preserve existing owners across a re-materialize and union the current run's owner in, rather than resetting; or, if resetting is deliberate for some reason, make the reset explicit and prove no sibling edge can exist at that point. Whichever is chosen, add a sensor that fails if a multi-owner resource loses an edge through a replace.
acceptance_criteria: A failing spec first demonstrates the clobber with a multi-owner fixture: a resource owned by two packs, replaced via the TASK-182 plugin-wins path, loses the sibling pack's owner edge. Capture the red-run output verbatim.
Owner edges belonging to other packs survive a re-materialize through executeInstall, on both the install and the replace paths.

The interaction with executeRemove's 'a still-owned resource is never deleted' guarantee is proven by a spec: after a replace by pack B, a resource still owned by pack A is not removable as an orphan.
The chosen approach (preserve-and-union vs. explicit reset with a proof no sibling edge can exist) is recorded in the closing comment with reasoning.
npm run test:all is green; no existing pack/reconcile/apply spec regresses; dist/pack-ctl.cjs rebuilt and committed if bundled source changes, with dist-parity passing.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body:
APPROVED and closed on a green FULL-depth review. **0 HIGH / 3 MEDIUM / 1 LOW.** Commit `a44e094`.

## AC4 — the decision, recorded here as the AC requires

**PRESERVE-AND-UNION, not reset-with-proof.** `executeInstall` now seeds the new lock entry's `owners` from `priorEntry.owners` (falling back to `[]` when there is none) and calls `addOwner` to union the current run's edge in, instead of hard-resetting to `[]`.

**Reasoning.** `dropOwner`/`isOrphaned` (`src/integrations-lock.js`) operate on whatever the array holds at call time with exact-string checks — neither requires a fresh reset. And `executeRemove`'s "a still-owned resource is never deleted" guarantee **depends on the opposite** of a reset: a dropped sibling edge makes that pack's resource look orphaned and removable in a later, unrelated run. Reset-with-proof was not available either — the condition that makes the drop live (two packs declaring the same resource id) is a schema-permitted shape, so "no sibling can exist here" cannot be proven in general.

## Red reproduced independently, not trusted

The reviewer extracted `src/` at both `f8bc84b` and `a44e094` into a sandbox and drove `applyPlan` with the RED-LOCK fixture. Pre-fix: owners after replace = `["watch@1.0.0"]` — design-power's edge clobbered. Post-fix: `["design-power@0.1.0","watch@1.0.0"]`. The tests-first invariant is proven mechanically.

## The fixture redesign was NOT concealment — checked, because it could have been

The developer's first AC3 test used two different `watch` owner-version strings and failed on a retained `watch@1.0.0`; it then held the pack's own owner identity constant so only the skill's pin bumps. *"I changed the test until it passed"* and *"I isolated the right concern"* look identical in a hand-off, so the reviewer verified rather than accepted: the redesigned fixture **still exercises the cross-pack clobber**, proven by the pre-fix red reproduction above. What it stopped exhibiting is the genuinely different same-pack version-bookkeeping concern — which is real, which is why it becomes a ticket rather than being quietly retired with the fixture.

## MEDIUM-1 — the residual is real, demonstrated, and now ticketed as TASK-202

Phantom same-pack version edges make a resource **permanently un-removable**. Reviewer's probe: prior owners `["design-power@0.1.0","watch@1.0.0"]`, replace executed by `watch@2.0.0` → owners become `["design-power@0.1.0","watch@1.0.0","watch@2.0.0"]`. After both `watch@2.0.0` and `design-power@0.1.0` remove, the entry survives with `["watch@1.0.0"]` and the live dir is still on disk — no reconciler flow can ever clear it, since `dropOwner` is exact-string and nothing parses pack-id from `pack-id@version`.

**Acceptable to land, not acceptable indefinitely.** The failure direction is retention, which is recoverable by a manual lock edit; the alternative the old code implemented was **deletion of a sibling's working skill**, which is not. And `plan()`'s removal candidacy already requires owners-empty (`src/pack-reconcile.js:231-234`), so no end-to-end reconcile flow reaches the stranding today — it bites only direct `applyPlan` callers. But phantom edges accumulate monotonically and quietly hollow out `executeRemove`'s contract. **TASK-202 minted.**

## MEDIUM-2 — a sibling instance the reviewer went looking for, in the WORSE direction

`src/assimilate.js:586-599`: `assimilateSkill` writes `owners: []` then `addOwner`. Re-assimilating a resource id already owned by another pack **silently drops the sibling's edge**, after which the assimilating pack's later remove deletes a resource the sibling still wants — exactly the failure mode this ticket's description names, in the data-loss direction rather than the retention direction. Pre-existing and outside `executeInstall`'s scope, so not a blocker here. **TASK-203 minted.**

## MEDIUM-3 discharged

The R3 checklist is present in the hand-off with all five items: unspecced path (read the fresh-install `hasPriorPin === false` and TASK-142 content-integrity branches; both unaffected since `priorOwners` falls back to `[]`, verified by pre-existing specs still passing); red-green planted; dist rebuilt (one bundle); parity n/a; calibration n/a.

## LOW

`src/pack-apply.js:449-450` — the decision comment says `dropOwner`/`isOrphaned` are "the only other readers of `owners[]`", but `plan()` also reads it via an inlined owners-empty check (`src/pack-reconcile.js:231-232`) and `assimilateSkill` writes it (`src/assimilate.js:593`). **The conclusion holds anyway** — neither depends on the reset — but the survey claim should be corrected next time the file is touched.

## Verified good

**AC3's spec proves the downstream guarantee, not the field** — it executes a real remove through `applyPlan` → `executeRemove` → `dropOwner`/`isOrphaned` and asserts on live-dir survival plus the on-disk lock, not merely array contents. (The remove op is hand-constructed, which is the right seam: `plan()` would never generate it, per the owners-empty precondition.)

**Latent-vs-live accurately stated, neither over- nor understated** — the two built-in descriptors declare disjoint skill ids, and the repo's own lockfile has only single-owner entries.

**dist:** only `dist/pack-ctl.cjs`; `bin/pack-ctl.js` is the sole entrypoint whose graph reaches `src/pack-apply.js` (all 8 checked). Parity green across all 8 — no build-environment signature.

## Gate

`test:since -- f8bc84b` 341/342 ⬛ `npm test` 1151/1152 ⬛ named e2e 59/59 including all-8-bundle dist-parity ⬛ `test:all` 2153/2158. The single failure in every run is TASK-198's pre-authorized red sensor, correctly not filed.
